newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares shake off U.S. woes, end slightly up.
newsitem.headline: German shares shake off U.S. woes, end slightly up.

text.p: German shares shook off one of the worst one-day declines on Wall Street to end bourse trade with modest gains on Tuesday.
The 30-share DAX index, which fell as low as 3,709.58 points in morning trade due to the 2.50 percent overnight drop on Wall Street, ended up 1.10 points at 3,755.82 points.
"People are thinking that the breakdown on Wall Street was just a one-day affair," said one Frankfurt dealer.
Wall Street stocks on Monday ended down sharply after Japan's Prime Minister Ryuto Hashimoto commented on the potential sale by Japan of U.S. government securities.
The bout of profit-taking was the second largest single-day point drop in the history of the Dow Jones index.
German traders said the DAX index found strong support near 3,700 points and few saw a chance of that level being broken in the near-term.
Instead, the DAX has begun to stabilise between 3,725 and 3,750 points as traders square up books ahead of the end of the second quarter.

"International investors do not appear to be interested in the German market right now," said one Frankfurt trader. "The action after the early selling pressure appears to be mainly from domestic investors looking for bargains."
One share attracting buying attention was electronics group Siemens AG, which ended bourse trade up 3.15 points at 106.35 marks on strong technical buying based on chart indicators.
"Siemens is withstanding the pressure very well and should keep outperforming the market," said one trader. "

German airline Lufthansa AG ended down 80 pfennigs at 34.60 marks ahead of its annual general meeting on Thursday. A Lufthansa official said on Monday in Hong Kong that the airline was talking with major airlines to build a cargo alliance.
